### Build Minutes [...] ### Build Minutes

Every deployment triggers a build process that compiles, tests, and packages your application. Build times vary by framework: a simple React app typically builds in 2-4 minutes, while a large Next.js project with many pages can take 10-20 minutes. At $0.01/minute beyond the free tier, even 5,000 build minutes per month only costs $40.

### Bandwidth and Storage

Data served covers all content delivered to users, including HTML, JavaScript, CSS, images, and API responses. At $0.15/GB, a site serving 100 GB/month costs $12.75 beyond the free tier. This is competitive with CloudFront pricing but simpler since Amplify bundles CDN distribution automatically. [...] Amplify Pricing Guide optimization checklist

Hosting a static website on AWS costs about $1 to $3 a month after the free tier, using S3 for storage and Route 53 for DNS. A dynamic site with a database and steady traffic runs higher, often $50 to a few hundred dollars a month, depending on compute and storage.

results.title: AWS Free Tier 2026: What's Included, Limits & Hidden Costs
results.content:
### Data Transfer Out Costs Money From the First Byte

You get 100 GB per month of free data transfer out across all services combined. After that, it's roughly $0.09 per GB. Downloading files from S3 to your laptop or serving traffic from EC2 both count toward this. It catches people who assume compute or storage free tiers cover bandwidth too.

### Elastic IP Addresses Charge When Unused

Elastic IPs (static public addresses) are free while attached to a running instance. If you allocate one and don't attach it — or stop the instance it's attached to — AWS charges $0.005 per hour. That's $3.60 per month for a forgotten IP address.

### Some Services Have No Free Tier [...] ### S3: Object Storage

5 GB of standard storage, 20,000 GET requests, and 2,000 PUT requests per month for 12 months. Good for static files and learning storage concepts. Note that data transfer out of S3 to the internet counts against the shared 100 GB per month free outbound bandwidth allowance.

### RDS: Relational Databases

750 hours per month of a db.t3.micro database for 12 months. MySQL, PostgreSQL, and MariaDB are all covered. Running two databases simultaneously exceeds the allowance by mid-month.

### Lambda: Serverless Functions

1 million requests and 400,000 GB-seconds of compute per month, always free. This is the most generous Free Tier allocation relative to what development workloads and small production APIs actually use. Most teams never exceed it. [...] ### Create an IAM User for Daily Work

Never use the root account for day-to-day tasks. Go to IAM → Users → Add users. Create a user with AdministratorAccess permissions and set up MFA for that user too. Sign out of root and use the IAM user from now on. Root credentials should stay locked away until you need them for account-level operations.

### Set Up Billing Alerts

Go to Billing Dashboard → Billing Preferences. Enable Free Tier usage alerts and Receive billing alerts. Then open CloudWatch → Alarms → Create Alarm. Set thresholds at $1, $5, and $10 so you catch overages before they compound.

💡 Pro tip: A $1 alert catches problems within hours. Most accidental runaway costs hit that threshold before anyone notices.

## Conclusion

The AWS Free Tier is more flexible than its predecessor, offering up to $200 in credits alongside more than 30 always-free services. Understanding how credits work, which services remain free, and what happens when your plan ends is the best way to avoid unexpected charges.

As your workloads grow beyond the AWS Free Tier, it's worth comparing pricing models across providers. While AWS offers Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, and Spot Instances, platforms such as Rackspace Spot provide another option for organizations looking to reduce compute costs through managed Kubernetes and an auction-based marketplace for Spot instances

‍

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does AWS have a free tier? [...] ### Does AWS have a free tier?

Yes. AWS Free Tier gives new accounts a choice between a Free plan and a Paid plan. Both start with $100 in credits, which can grow to $200 by completing onboarding activities, and both include access to more than 30 always-free services with permanent monthly usage limits.

‍

### What is AWS Free Tier?

AWS Free Tier is Amazon's program for exploring AWS services without paying upfront. Since July 15, 2025, new accounts choose between a Free plan and a Paid plan, both funded by sign-up credits and supported by a collection of always-free services.

‍

### How do I get AWS Free Tier? [...] ‍

### After July 15, 2025

 Choose between a Free plan or a Paid plan during signup
 Receive $100 in credits, with up to $100 more available by completing five onboarding activities:
  + Launch and terminate an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance
  + Configure an Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) database
  + Deploy an AWS Lambda function
  + Test a prompt in Amazon Bedrock
  + Create a budget alert in AWS Budgets
 The Free plan lasts for 6 months or until your credits are exhausted, after which the account closes automatically
 The Paid plan provides access to all AWS services and switches to standard pay-as-you-go pricing after credits are used
 More than 30 always-free services remain available under both plans
